stem: Which postal service lets a business pay for its customers' replies, using reply cards it supplies?

options.content: Business reply service
options.rationale: Correct: customers post the pre-printed card free.

options.content: Poste restante
options.rationale: Poste restante holds mail for collection.

options.content: Registered mail
Cash on delivery service
options.rationale: Cash on delivery collects payment for goods.

explanation: With **business reply service**, the business supplies pre-printed cards or envelopes and pays the postage when they are returned.

options.content: Mail held at a post office until the receiver collects it
A machine that prints the postage on a firm's envelopes
A service that collects payment on delivery
Priority delivery of letters for an extra charge

explanation: Poste restante: mail is kept at a named post office for collection, useful for people without a fixed address.

stem: A business sells goods to a new customer it does not know and wants to be sure of payment. Which service should it use?

options.content: Cash on delivery
options.rationale: Correct: payment is collected before the goods are handed over.

options.content: Freepost
Poste restante
options.rationale: This holds mail for collection; it does not collect payment.

options.content: A franking machine

explanation: With cash on delivery the agent collects payment from the buyer on delivery.

stem: Why would a business send a signed contract by registered mail rather than ordinary post?

options.content: It is always cheaper than ordinary post
It allows the receiver to reply free of charge
It is recorded, signed for and compensated if lost
It is collected from the post office by travellers

explanation: Registered mail gives security, proof of delivery and compensation for valuable or important items.

stem: Which is the main advantage of a franking machine to a business that sends many letters?

options.content: It delivers the letters directly to customers' doors
options.rationale: Franking prints postage; delivery is still by the post.

options.content: It saves buying and sticking stamps and controls postage costs
It guarantees full compensation if any letters are lost
It lets customers reply without paying postage
options.rationale: That is business reply or freepost.

explanation: A franking machine prints postage on envelopes; the business pays in advance and keeps a record of postage used.

stem: A firm in Harare must deliver tender documents to an office in Bulawayo by tomorrow morning. Which service is most suitable?

options.content: Ordinary letter post
Poste restante
A courier service
options.rationale: Correct: fast, door to door, tracked.

options.content: Business reply service

explanation: Courier services suit urgent, important items between towns, despite their higher cost.
hints: Which service is fastest and delivers to the door?

stem: Why do many businesses in rural areas use a PO Box address?

options.content: PO Boxes deliver parcels and letters to the door
options.rationale: Mail must be collected from the box.

options.content: PO Boxes are a free service at every post office
Couriers are not allowed to deliver to any of the rural areas
options.rationale: Couriers may not cover remote areas, but they are not banned.

options.content: There may be no street delivery, and a box gives a secure address

explanation: A post office box gives a fixed, secure address where there is no delivery to premises.
hints: Think about where mail is delivered.

stem: Which is a disadvantage of postal services compared with email?

options.content: They cannot carry goods or parcels
They give no proof of delivery for any item
options.rationale: Registered and recorded services give proof.

options.content: They do not reach rural areas at all
options.rationale: The national postal service reaches many rural areas.

options.content: They are slower and feedback takes days

explanation: Post is slower and gives no instant feedback; email is instant but cannot carry goods.

stem: Courier companies usually collect and deliver items door to door.
explanation: True. This is one of their main advantages over ordinary post.

stem: Recorded delivery pays full compensation if a valuable item is lost.
explanation: False. Recorded delivery mainly proves posting and delivery; **registered mail** gives compensation for loss.

stem: Match each business need with the most suitable postal service.

left.content: Sending a certificate that must not be lost
Encouraging customers to return a survey form free of charge
Receiving letters while travelling between towns
Sending 500 letters without sticking stamps on each
Selling goods by post to a new customer

explanation: Each service meets a particular business need.

stem: Name the private businesses that deliver documents and parcels quickly door to door, often with tracking.
explanation: **Courier companies** offer fast, tracked, door-to-door delivery.

stem: A firm's franking machine records 450 letters posted at US\$0.35 each. Calculate the total postage.

An online seller sends 24 parcels a month. Courier delivery costs US\$8.50 a parcel and parcel post costs US\$3.25. Calculate how much more the seller pays each month by using the courier for all parcels.
explanation: Difference per parcel = US\$8.50 − US\$3.25 = US\$5.25. × 24 = US\$126.
workedSolution:
1. Extra per parcel = 8.50 − 3.25 = 5.25.
2. Extra per month = 5.25 × 24 = US\$126.
hints: Find the difference per parcel, then multiply by the number of parcels.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why postal services are still important to businesses even though email is widely used.

points.description: Goods / parcels must be physically delivered.
Online orders still need delivery to customers.
Original signed documents / certificates / reaching people without internet.
Explained: email cannot carry originals; some rural customers have no internet but have a PO Box.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Email cannot carry goods, so businesses that sell online still need parcel post or couriers to deliver orders. Original signed contracts and certificates must also be sent physically, and some customers in rural areas can only be reached through a post office box.

explanation: Physical delivery, originals and reach to people without internet keep postal services important.

stem: Thandeka runs a mail-order business in Bulawayo selling seeds to small-scale farmers across Zimbabwe. Farmers find her through radio adverts and order by post or by phone. Many farmers live far from towns and collect mail from post offices at rural service centres.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which service would let farmers send order forms to Thandeka without paying postage, using envelopes she supplies?

options.content: Poste restante
Business reply service
Recorded delivery service
Express mail
options.rationale: This is faster delivery for a fee.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why the national postal service may suit Thandeka better than a courier company for most deliveries.

points.description: Wide network reaching rural service centres.
Couriers may not deliver to remote areas.
Lower cost per parcel.
Seeds are light and not usually urgent, so speed matters less.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain how cash on delivery could help Thandeka's business.

points.description: Farmers pay when the seeds are delivered / collected.
Thandeka is sure of payment, no bad debts.
Farmers trust ordering from a distant seller they have not met, so more orders.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Discuss **one** problem Thandeka may face from relying on postal services, and how she could reduce it.

points.description: Problem identified, e.g. delays during the planting season / loss or damage.
Effect: seeds arrive too late to plant, complaints, lost customers.
Solution, e.g. send early / registered or tracked parcels / courier for urgent orders.
Judgement on how far the solution works (cost).

explanation: The postal network reaches rural farmers cheaply; COD secures payment; delays and losses must be managed.
hints: (d) Think about timing in the farming season.

stem: Some people say that the national postal service will soon disappear because people now communicate by email and messaging apps.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **two** services, other than delivering letters, offered by a post office.

points.description: One service, e.g. PO Box / private bag.
Another, e.g. parcel post / money transfer / registered mail / express mail / poste restante.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** ways in which email and messaging have affected postal services.

points.description: Fewer letters posted.
So lower revenue from letter post / fewer post offices or staff.
More online shopping.
So more parcels to deliver / growth of courier and parcel services.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Discuss whether postal services will disappear.

points.description: Letter volumes are falling as people use email and messaging.
Couriers compete for parcels.
But online shopping increases parcel deliveries.
Rural areas and people without internet still rely on post.
Original documents and goods must still be carried; post offices can add new services.
Justified conclusion.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Letter post has fallen sharply as people use email and messaging, and couriers compete for urgent parcels. However, online shopping has created more parcels to deliver, and many people in rural areas without internet still rely on post offices and PO Boxes. Goods and original documents cannot be emailed. Postal services are therefore unlikely to disappear, but they must change, focusing on parcels, payment services and rural coverage rather than letters.

explanation: Electronic communication has reduced letters but online trade has increased parcels; postal services are changing rather than disappearing.
hints: (c) Weigh falling letters against growing parcels and rural needs.
